tests.error: ContractError: target mount boundary was not reached

verified_repairs: The original R2 cross-mount defect is corrected for correctly specified paths: independent present and absent probes passed on root-backed /tmp and /dev/shm tmpfs.
Wrong target mount ID and wrong device were rejected on both filesystems.
The authenticated boundary selects the first exact device+mount-ID match and requires every descendant to remain on that mount.
Checked-in pre-boundary identity substitution, symlink, simulated nested bind, late mount-ID rebound and parent replacement attacks reject.
The exact schemas, resource and inode floors, watcher requirements, checkpoint guard, pending authority, frozen hashes and downstream G1/G2 locks from R2 remain intact.

release_blockers.finding: The focused checked-in suite is not green in either interpreter. The legacy absent-cache test creates its path under the verifier worktree but supplies Path('/').st_dev instead of the actual target filesystem device; when the clean worktree is on a separate mount, the authenticated boundary correctly cannot be reached.
evidence: test_trn22_tmpfs_package.py:618-625 errors in default and Torch runs.
Both runs report ContractError: target mount boundary was not reached.
release_blockers.impact: The required full focused regression suite is not portable or releasable from a clean verifier worktree.
release_blockers.minimal_repair: Make the root-backed fixture derive both expected device and mount ID from its actual chosen parent, while keeping the explicit /dev/shm cross-mount cases. Require all checked-in suites to pass from a clean detached worktree.

release_blockers.finding: snapshot_tree performs its final lexical chain validation before snapshot_tree_revalidate, but does not revalidate the chain or returned manifest after that reseal call. Mutation or rebinding at the final reseal-return boundary therefore produces a stale PASS receipt.
evidence: Independent same-inode attack changed a sealed 4-byte file from AAAA to BBBB after snapshot_tree_revalidate completed; snapshot_path returned PASS with the old SHA-256 while the live file held BBBB.

Independent rebound attack renamed the sealed target directory and created a replacement with attacker bytes after snapshot_tree_revalidate completed; snapshot_path returned PASS describing the displaced old directory while the authorized lexical target pointed to the replacement.
storage_contract.py:705 performs the last chain check, lines 725-729 reseal then return without a post-reseal chain/name/manifest validation.
release_blockers.impact: Root-cache or tmpfs output/cache evidence can authenticate bytes and inode identities no longer present at the authorized lexical path, allowing a late cache write or target replacement to false-pass adjudication.
release_blockers.minimal_repair: Make the terminal seal jointly bind the pinned chain, lexical names, exact recursive membership and same-descriptor bytes through return. At minimum revalidate the full mount-aware chain after the recursive reseal and ensure no intervening unvalidated boundary remains; add deterministic same-inode same-size post-reseal mutation and target-directory rebound tests at every final-seal boundary.
